title: Smooth fixed subschemes of semisimple elements
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A point $s\in H(k)$ is semisimple if its image under every finite-dimensional algebraic representation $H\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is diagonalizable; an algebraic representation is a homomorphism of group schemes, $V$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and $\operatorname{GL}(V)(A)$ is the group of invertible $A$-linear maps on $V\otimes_k A$. Let $H$ be smooth and connected, let $X$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $a:H\times_k X\to X$ be an action, meaning a morphism satisfying $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(h_1h_2,x)=a(h_1,a(h_2,x))$ after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. Products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $s\in H(k)$ be semisimple and let $X^s$ be the closed subscheme equalizing $a(s,-):X\to X$ and $\mathrm{id}_X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $X^s(A)=\{x\in X(A):a(s_A,x)=x\}$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Then $X^s$ is smooth over $k$. No connectedness assumption on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 13.8, printed p.257, smoothness assertion, specialized to a smooth connected acting affine group and a smooth affine scheme.

proof.text: Put $\Gamma=\{s^n:n\in\mathbf Z\}$. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-cyclic-closure-linearly-reductive], its reduced Zariski closure $G\hookrightarrow H$ is a smooth affine finite-type closed subgroup, is linearly reductive, and contains the Zariski-dense subgroup $\Gamma\subset G(k)$. The hypothesis on $s$ is precisely the representation criterion in that lemma; no characteristic-zero or connectedness hypothesis on $G$ is needed. Restrict the given action along $G\hookrightarrow H$; its two action laws follow by substitution into those of the original action.

source.place: Corollary 13.8, printed p.257, proof; application of Theorem 13.7, printed p.256.

proof.text: For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, a point $x\in X(A)$ fixed by $s_A$ is fixed by every $s_A^n$: nonnegative powers follow by induction using the action law, and $s_A^{-1}x=x$ follows by applying $s_A^{-1}$ to $s_Ax=x$. Conversely, being fixed by all powers includes $n=1$. Hence the given closed equalizer $X^s\hookrightarrow X$ represents exactly the common-fixed-point functor of $\Gamma$ for the restricted $G$-action. This argument works for nonreduced $A$ as well, so it identifies the scheme functors, not just their $k$-points.

source.place: Corollary 13.8, printed p.257, proof; application of Theorem 13.7, printed p.256.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-linearly-reductive-dense-fixed-smooth] with $G$, $\Gamma$, the restricted action on the original smooth affine finite-type scheme $X$, and $F=X^s$. Step 1 supplies smoothness and linear reductivity of $G$ and density of $\Gamma$; step 2 supplies the required representation of its common-fixed-point functor by the specified closed subscheme. The conclusion is that $X^s$ is smooth over $k$. The lemma permits disconnected $X$ and also covers an empty fixed scheme.

The item's statement, stmt_deps and source match live byte for byte, and live still has the item unsplit with no copies of the new nodes; there is no repair note. The split follows Milne's two-step proof of 13.8. Step 1 cites the cyclic-closure node, whose hypotheses H affine finite type and s semisimple hold, and gives G closed, smooth and linearly reductive with Gamma dense. Step 2 is elementary: fixed by s equals fixed by every power, checked over every algebra A, so X^s represents the Gamma-fixed functor. Step 3 cites the dense-fixed node with every input checked; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The cyclic-closure node is true by Milne 1.40/1.45/1.26 (reduced closure is a smooth subgroup) and 9.19 (s is semisimple in a faithful representation restricted to G, hence in all), with Milne's argument that s-stable equals G-stable. I tested s=1, finite order prime to p (disconnected G), a torus, and characteristic p (no mu_p). The dense-fixed node is Milne Lemma 13.6/13.7 with S=Gamma; I checked it independently: Gamma dense in reduced G gives X^Gamma=X^G, then Iversen/Fogarty. Linear reductivity is kept, which is needed by Milne 13.13. On duplicates: lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth covers tori only and is not enough, because the cyclic closure can be Z/m times a torus; the 13.2/13.3 regular-ring nodes are inputs for the later split, and nothing else matches.
